title: Prompt template canonicalization and slot-packing for cross-request cache deduplication
creator: Marisol Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's serving runtime currently stores per-request KV cache slices keyed by raw prompt tokens or naive prefix substrings. This leads to a proliferation of near-duplicate cache entries for semantically equivalent prompt templates (minor var substitutions, whitespace differences, separators), causing low reuse, increased GPU memory pressure, and suboptimal batching behavior.

Goal:
Create a canonicalization and packing pipeline that turns incoming prompt templates into normalized 'template slots' with compact, collision-aware fingerprints and pack small canonical segments into token-slabs that align with the GPU allocator. The system should increase cross-request cache hit rate, reduce GPU memory fragmentation, and integrate with the continuous batcher so repeated templates are collocated into the same batch shards when possible.

Scope and non-goals:
- In-scope: canonicalization rules, stable fingerprint format, slot assignment, slab packing strategy, eviction scoring update, continuous-batcher hinting for collocation, migration tool to compact existing cache entries.
- Out-of-scope: model-side tokenizer changes, customer-visible prompt rewriting, or global config UI (console work tracked separately).

Motivation metrics to improve:
- KV cache effective reuse rate (target +30% relative to baseline for high-similarity workloads).
- GPU memory fragmentation metric (reduce wasted pages by 20%).
- Average per-request latency for warm-cached templates (<= +5ms change).
- Serving cost per 1M tokens for workloads with heavy template repetition (target -12%).
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalization module accepts prompt + stable metadata and emits deterministic canonical template id (fingerprint) with namespace versioning
Slot-packing groups canonical segments into slab-sized allocations so that small segments share page-aligned GPU memory with maximum packing efficiency >= 85% in synthetic packing microbenchmarks
Continuous-batcher uses template id hints to prefer co-location and demonstrates at least 20% increase in same-batch coalescing for repeated templates in integration tests
Migration job can scan selected KV namespaces and rewrite entries to new canonical ids without service downtime (can be run incrementally)
End-to-end e2e test shows +25-40% cache hit rate on three realistic prompt corpora (support bot, transactional email, search-rerank) compared to baseline
No customer-facing regressions: throughput and p50 latency within 10% of baseline under load tests
Telemetry added: per-template hit/miss counters, slab utilization, fragmentation percentage, and rolling regression alerts in Console
design_notes:
High-level design:
1) Canonicalization rules and normalization: whitespace normalization, canonical punctuation for common separators, placeholder detection for small alphanumeric tokens (email-like, UUID-ish) turned into positional placeholders, and optional deterministic min-hashing for very long templated sections. Rules are implemented as a composable pipeline with explicit transforms and unit tests for each rule.

2) Fingerprinting: use a two-part id: short stable namespace v1 prefix (e.g., TPLv1) + 64-bit BLAKE3 truncated digest of the canonical template. The digest is collision-resistant for practical workloads and short enough for indexing. Include a human-readable short-hash for debugging (not used as primary key). Versioning allows future changes to canonicalization rules without invalidating older entries.

3) Slot and slab packing: canonical templates are decomposed into segments (e.g., static chunks between placeholders). Each segment is considered a 'slot'. Slots below a threshold (e.g., 256 tokens) are coalesced into slabs sized for the GPU allocator (e.g., page multiples of 2560 tokens or 8KB-equivalent). Slab metadata stores slot offsets and lengths. This reduces per-slot allocation overhead and reduces fragmentation.

4) GPU allocator integration: extend the allocator to support slab objects with internal slot indexing. Slabs are reference-counted and can be partially evicted or compacted. The allocator exposes APIs for fast slot lookup by (template_id, slot_index) to retrieve KV fragments.

5) Continuous-batcher changes: when enqueuing requests, compute template fingerprint early and add a collocation hint to the request object. The batcher shards in-memory queues by hashed (model, template_fingerprint % N) when latency SLO allows, increasing chance of cache hits within the same micro-batch. Fall back to existing heuristics under high tail latency.

6) Eviction policy: new scoring function incorporates slot co-usage frequency, slab packing density, and size-aware LRU. Priority given to evicting slabs with low co-usage and high fragmentation. Implement safe background compaction to reduce live-set fragmentation.

7) Migration and compatibility: provide a sidecar migration process that scans legacy KV namespaces and emits canonical entries into new namespaces. During migration read path will check new namespace first then fallback to old keys and perform on-read rewrite. This ensures zero downtime migration and gradual adoption.

8) Observability: add per-template histograms for hits, misses, average slot size, slab occupancy, and compaction run stats. Surface top-N templates by memory consumption and hit-rate in Console dashboards.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging): implement canonicalization + fingerprint generation behind runtime flag; pack-only path simulated (no writes) and collect telemetry (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (canary): enable write-path for small percentage of traffic and run migration tool on canary namespaces (2 weeks). Monitor hit-rate, latency, slab utilization, and roll back on regressions.
Phase 3 (gradual): increase traffic to 25% then 75% over two weeks, run background compactions nightly, and validate migration coverage.
Phase 4 (full): enable by default and deprecate legacy KV namespace; schedule final compaction and storage reclaim.
Rollback strategy: feature-flag off triggers immediate stop of new writes and batcher collocation hints; fallback read semantics already handle old-key reads.
Communication: coordinate with Console team for telemetry queries and with Solutions for any enterprise customers asking about deterministic behavior.
tests_and_validation:
Unit tests for canonicalization transforms with coverage for edge-cases (unicode, mixed encodings, long sequences).
Microbenchmarks: packing efficiency test harness that simulates slot distributions and measures GPU page utilization.
Integration tests: synthetic traffic generator producing repeated template distributions to assert cache hit uplift and batching coalescing.
Load tests: run full qps replay on staging cluster for 48h, assert p50/p95/p99 latency, error rates, and memory usage.
Safety tests: collision-injection tests (force same fingerprint for different templates) to ensure correctness fallback (secondary checksum verification) and safe isolation.
notes:
Design trade-offs: heavy canonicalization risks false negatives if user-visible prompts are intentionally different; we mitigate by versioned namespaces and conservative placeholdering. We prefer minimal rewrite semantics at first and expand transforms only after observation.
Open questions: optimal slab size across different GPU families, whether to expose slot hints in SDK, and compaction frequency tuning.
Owners: Diego Morales (engineer) and Marisol Chen (tech lead).
